p: When you're staying for a few nights, the Blue Lagoon is less of a one-off trip and more of a daily treat. Plenty of families find a short morning or late-afternoon dip works better than one marathon session, as tired little swimmers turn grumpy fast. Pop in when it's raining, head out exploring when it's dry, and you'll get the best of both worlds across your break.

A few bits make life easier: a towel for each person, swim nappies for babies, goggles for the kids who hate splashes in their eyes, and a warm hoodie for the walk back to the lodge. If anyone's a nervous swimmer, start in Nippers Cove or the shallows of the wave pool and build up gently before tackling the flumes. Check the slide age and height rules with the lifeguards when you arrive so nobody's disappointed at the top of the steps.

Beyond the resort gates, there's a load of Pembrokeshire within easy reach. Folly Farm, with its zoo, farm and vintage funfair, is only a short drive away and is a firm favourite with families. Tenby's pastel-coloured harbour and sandy beaches are close too, and Saundersfoot is a smaller, gentler seaside village for a paddle and an ice cream. Pack a picnic, follow a stretch of the Pembrokeshire Coast Path, and the water park becomes the perfect wind-down at the end of the day.
